title: Reading a mini-Prolog solver
description: You can trace how terms, substitutions and clauses feed a depth-first search.

steps.description: Var represents a variable, Atom a named constant and Compound a functor with arguments. You store variable bindings in a substitution dictionary.
walk follows existing bindings. unify extends a substitution when terms match, using occurs to reject a variable inside its own proposed binding.
Clause holds a head and body goals. fresh creates renamed variables for a clause, while DB stores facts and rules as clauses.

steps.question: When unification succeeds, which goals does solve try next?
steps.answer: It places the fresh clause's body before the remaining goals and recursively searches with the new substitution.

steps.description: query gathers reified bindings, meaning terms with their substitutions applied. You populate the database with family facts and ancestor, member and append clauses.
The driver requests ancestor, descendant and list relations. The supplied capped recording prints only the ancestors-of-jim heading, so you have no recorded bindings to inspect here.
